title: Implement Pro-Tier SVG Palette Export with Watermarking
description: ChromaticQuiver, a mobile utility for managing color palettes, aims to introduce a new premium feature to increase revenue. The task is to implement a new export option that allows users to save their color palettes as Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) files. This feature will be gated for 'Pro' tier subscribers. Non-Pro users will be able to export, but the resulting SVG file will contain a watermark. This task requires incremental development across multiple sessions, touching data models, business logic (use cases), and service adapters.

project_spec.name: ChromaticQuiver
project_spec.description:
ChromaticQuiver is a hard-level mobile utility written in C that transforms any smartphone into a real-time color-and-content capture studio. Users point the camera at the world to "shoot" colors, textures, and contextual metadata, instantly building a living palette quiver that can be tagged, merged, and exported to social networks or creative suites. The app safeguards personal collections with biometric authentication, synchronises edits while offline, and pushes curated inspiration via notifications, all wrapped in a responsive UI that adapts from tiny screens to folding devices.

Under the hood, ChromaticQuiver applies Clean Architecture to keep the creative core insulated from volatile platform concerns. The domain layer focuses on colour science, palette math, and in-app purchase entitlements, while data sources (local SQLite cache, remote REST + GraphQL endpoints) are integrated through repositories and adapter patterns. A pluggable analytics/crash-reporting module continuously feeds anonymised usage data to improve palette recommendations, and a factory-based camera pipeline lets developers drop in third-party lens or AR extensions without touching the business rules.
dependencies: mbedtls or OpenSSL (secure storage + biometric_auth hand-shake wrapper)
libuv (cross-platform async event loop supporting MVVM bindings)
